key_insight: A hierarchical reinforcement learning policy can decouple stable joint control from gait adaptation, enabling energy-efficient quadruped locomotion that automatically changes gait with speed.
engineering_relevance: The approach is directly relevant to real-world legged robots because it improves cost of transport, robustness, and sim-to-real transfer across flat, rough, and inclined terrain.
method: High-frequency low-level policy handles stable, robust joint motion execution.
Low-frequency high-level policy adapts gait to minimize cost of transport.
Three-stage Isaac-based training supports zero-shot transfer to a Unitree AlienGo.
evidence_signal: The authors evaluate the method in simulation against single-policy and hierarchical baselines across a broad range of commanded velocities and terrains, and also demonstrate zero-shot deployment on hardware.
watch_item: Results may depend on careful reward shaping and training setup, and hardware performance could still be sensitive to real-world dynamics not fully captured in simulation.
paper_title: Energy-Efficient Gait Adaptation via Hierarchical Reinforcement Learning for Quadrupedal Locomotion Across Diverse Terrains
